newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - EDS sinks after weak Q1. [CORRECTED 14:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - EDS sinks after weak Q1. [CORRECTED 14:50 GMT]

text.p: Electronic Data Systems Corp shares sank more than 17 percent in pre-opening trade on Friday after the computer services company said late on Thursday that first quarter profits fell 11 percent.

The Plano, Texas company said it was taking a close look at its staffing levels after it posted earnings per share of $0.40 a share, about 20 percent short of analysts' expectations, compared to $0.45 last year.
Shares of EDS were at 34-1/2, down from their New York Stock Exchange close of 42. The stock was also downgraded by Smith Barney on Friday, according to a source.
Other technology stocks falling ahead of the opening of trading were Intel Corp, Xilinx Inc, and Gateway 2000 Inc fell in pre-opening trading.
Gateway 2000 shares sank 2-3/4 from their Nasdaq close of 58-3/8, giving up a nearly 3 point run-up posted yesterday ahead of the release of the personal computer marketer's first quarter earnings.
Although the $0.86 a share quarterly earnings were in line with estimates, traders said whisper numbers had been "up in the 90's".

Another tech stock shaved after weaker-than-expected earnings was Xilinx, with the offer price falling to $50 from its close of 51-1/4. It earned $0.38 a share, versus the First Call analysts' consensus estimate of $0.36. (Corrects EPS figure and estimate).
Intel shares were also trading lower, losing 1-1/4 to at 144-7/8, a trader said.
